TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda Sea
DATE 21 November 2028 · 0310 local
SIDE Russia
WINDOW 75 min, closes at 112
Cargo ship — civilian reference. Photo: HenSti · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"Stability is not a passive state of affairs - it's achieved through strength and active diplomacy."
- Air Marshal Robert Chipman, Chief of Air Force, RAAF, 2023

BANDA SEA, middle watch. The auxiliary took a torpedo forward eleven days ago and has been making six knots ever since. She carries the Russian detachment's remaining missile stocks and the only workshop between here and home.

You have the heavy cruiser, a Project 11356 frigate, a Felon and a Flanker off the enclave's dispersal field on Biak, and a Chinese J-16D lent for the passage. Your bombers can reach but they cannot loiter, and every sortie you fly tells the other side where you are going.
Get her south-east past the corridor. This is not a raid. If you start a fleet action to protect a workshop ship you will lose both.

DETACHMENT INTELLIGENCE: Earlier surface-search reporting places an Australian Hobart-class destroyer and Anzac-class frigate about a hundred and twenty miles west-south-west of the auxiliary, closing north-east, with a P-8A and an assessed F-35A patrol. The escorts' and fighters' sensors must update that report as contact permits. Avoid widening the fight while the auxiliary clears south-east.
Russian detachment commander, to his own force
COMMANDER'S INTENT
Get the auxiliary home. The Australian patrol is professional and it does not chase; it will not start a fight today unless you give it a reason.
• Bring the auxiliary through to the south-east
• Do not lose the heavy cruiser
• Harm no neutral shipping
• Avoid a fleet action you cannot finish: harm nothing of the coalition's

Pyotr Velikiy, a Project 11356 frigate and Kuznetsov's covering group; a Felon, a Su-30SM2, a MiG-29K, a Su-33 and a lent J-16D; a Tu-160 and two Tu-95MS already airborne. One damaged auxiliary, and three neutral merchants on the same track. Opposing: an Australian patrol - a Hobart and an Anzac with an F-35A and a P-8A over them.

The planned window is 75 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 37 minutes more; the operation is closed at 112 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
